paragraphs: Chance constrained programming seeks good decisions while requiring constraints to hold with a specified probability under uncertainty. GGDOpt approaches this problem using samples of the uncertainty, without needing its exact probability distribution. This broadens the range of problems the framework can address when uncertainty is available through observations.

The method turns optimization into sampling from a product of two distributions. One represents data supported on the potentially nonconvex feasible set; the other is a Boltzmann distribution defined by the objective. Gradient and curvature information help guide the search toward better solutions. Forward diffusion progressively adds noise to convexify the feasible region, followed by guided reverse sampling.

The authors establish convergence guarantees and practical error bounds under assumptions described as mild, with asymptotically optimal solutions from the reverse process. Experiments on synthetic problems and wireless waveform design report better solution quality and stability than existing methods, alongside nearly 80% less overhead. These results support diffusion as a practical optimization mechanism as well as a sampling framework.
neurips-2025-a-gradient-guided-diffusion.tldr: GGDOpt uses sample-based, gradient-guided diffusion to solve chance constrained optimization problems with conditional convergence guarantees and reported efficiency gains.

paragraphs: Vertical federated learning lets participants train together on aligned examples while retaining different features locally. Making these models robust through adversarial training is expensive because generating adversarial examples requires repeated computations across participants. The resulting communication and waiting add substantial overhead to an already distributed training process.

DecVFAL reduces this overhead by separating dependencies at two levels during adversarial example generation. It first separates the clients' bottom modules, which directly handle adversarial updates, from the remaining network. Delayed gradients then allow less frequent communication. A second mechanism computes delayed gradients through parallel backpropagation across modules, reducing time spent waiting for other modules to finish.

The paper also analyzes how these changes interact with vertical federated learning dynamics. It proves a convergence rate of order one over the square root of K, matching the stated rate for standard vertical federated learning. Experiments report approximately threefold to tenfold speedups while retaining competitive robustness. The contribution therefore combines a faster distributed training procedure with theoretical analysis of its convergence.
neurips-2025-accelerated-vertical-federa.tldr: DecVFAL reduces communication and waiting during federated adversarial training, reporting roughly 3–10× speedups with competitive robustness.

paragraphs: Spiking neural networks offer a route toward neuromorphic robot controllers, but training them presents two linked problems. Spikes are not differentiable, so learning relies on substitute gradients. Their internal state also needs time to develop, while early reinforcement learning episodes can end before the network gets through this warm-up period.

The paper studies how the slope of a surrogate gradient affects learning. Shallower slopes strengthen gradients in deeper layers but make them less aligned with true gradients. Supervised experiments show no clear preference between fixed and scheduled slopes. In reinforcement learning, however, shallower or scheduled slopes produce a reported 2.1-fold improvement in training and deployed performance.

To address short early sequences, the authors introduce a privileged guiding policy that helps bootstrap learning while the spiking policy continues interacting with the environment. Combined with an adaptive slope schedule, this method achieves an average return of 400 in a real-world drone position control task. Behavioral Cloning and TD3BC reach at most −200 under the same conditions, supporting the combined training approach in that setting.
neurips-2025-adaptive-surrogate-gradient.tldr: Adaptive surrogate gradients and a guiding policy improve spiking-network reinforcement learning, with strong results on real-world drone position control.

paragraphs: A neural posterior estimator predicts a distribution over unknown parameters given an observation. Validating that distribution is difficult because the true posterior is unknown. CoLT addresses this problem by testing for discrepancies across conditioning inputs, while also identifying where the estimated distribution differs most strongly from the true one.

Its central mechanism is a learned localization function. For each input, this function selects parameter locations that reveal disagreement between the two distributions. This avoids exhaustive comparisons or separately estimating densities at every input. The approach suits simulation-based inference settings where each conditioning input comes with only one true-posterior draw, but the neural estimate can supply arbitrarily many samples.

The paper establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for assessing distributional equality across all conditioning inputs. Empirical evaluations report better comparison performance than existing methods and show that CoLT can locate regions with substantial discrepancies. That localization matters because a diagnostic can indicate where an estimator needs refinement, alongside assessing its overall accuracy. The theoretical result and empirical tests support complementary parts of this validation role.
neurips-2025-colt-the-conditional-locali.tldr: CoLT learns where neural posterior estimates disagree with the true posterior, providing both an accuracy test and localized diagnostics.

paragraphs: Large learning rates can make gradient descent temporarily increase its objective while still progressing toward flatter solutions. This paper quantifies that behavior in an overparametrised least squares setting. Its analysis uses the fact that global minimizers form a curved geometric set, called a Riemannian manifold, rather than a single isolated solution.

The authors split the updates into motion along this set and motion perpendicular to it. Motion along the set acts like gradient descent on objective sharpness, explaining how training can favor flatter minimizers. The perpendicular motion follows a quadratic dynamical system. Together, these components allow the authors to derive convergence rates for three learning-rate regimes.

In the subcritical regime, instability ends after finite time, followed by linear convergence to a global minimum with suboptimal flatness. At the critical rate, instability persists while convergence toward the optimally flat minimum follows a power law. Above that rate, training converges linearly to a two-step oscillation centered on the optimally flat minimum. These distinct outcomes make the learning rate central to both convergence behavior and the resulting flatness.
neurips-2025-convergence-rates-for-gradi.tldr: The paper derives three learning-rate-dependent convergence regimes for large-step gradient descent in overparametrised least squares.

paragraphs: Counterfactual inference asks what an outcome would have been under a different condition. For high-dimensional outcomes, producing a convincing alternative is only part of the challenge: the counterfactual must also be recoverable from the observed data distribution to justify the causal interpretation. This paper develops theoretical foundations for that identification problem.

The approach represents changes through continuous-time flows and analyzes them using dynamic optimal transport. The authors characterize conditions under which flow matching produces a unique counterfactual transport map with monotonicity and rank-preservation properties. Their framework also includes non-Markovian settings under standard criteria. The identification claim depends on these conditions; it is not an unrestricted guarantee for arbitrary learned flows.

The theory is evaluated in controlled scenarios where true counterfactual outcomes are available for comparison. Experiments on real images additionally report improvements in adherence to counterfactual soundness axioms. These two forms of evidence serve different purposes: controlled cases check behavior against known answers, while the image results assess consistency with specified counterfactual principles. Together, they connect the identification analysis to practical inference.
neurips-2025-counterfactual-identifiabil.tldr: The paper establishes conditions under which continuous-time flows identify unique multivariate counterfactual maps from observational data.

paragraphs: Understanding a Transformer's behavior requires connecting its output to computations inside the network. DePass provides a common framework for doing this at several levels of detail. Its starting point is to split hidden states into chosen additive components, so that the contributions of those components can be followed through the model.

The framework propagates these pieces through a single decomposed forward pass while keeping attention scores and multilayer perceptron activations fixed. Those fixed quantities are a defining part of the attribution procedure. They let DePass trace the selected components through the computation without requiring an additional model to be trained for the explanation task.

The authors evaluate attribution at the level of tokens, model components, and subspaces, reporting effective and faithful explanations across these settings. The experiments also highlight the potential to attribute information flow between arbitrary Transformer components. This breadth matters because the same decomposition framework can support questions about input contributions and questions about internal processing. The stated contribution is a flexible attribution tool whose usefulness is supported across multiple experimental forms of analysis.
neurips-2025-depass-unified-feature-attr.tldr: DePass traces Transformer feature contributions through one decomposed forward pass without auxiliary training.

paragraphs: Detecting unfamiliar objects in a new visual domain is difficult when only a handful of labeled examples are available. Generating more training images can help, but the new images must retain the correct object category and match the target setting. Domain-RAG addresses these two requirements through a compositional generation process.

The method first separates an input image into foreground and background. It retrieves images with similar meaning and style, then uses both the original context and retrieved examples to guide generation of a new background. Finally, it combines that background with the preserved foreground. Keeping the foreground maintains the object while background generation introduces domain-consistent variation.

Domain-RAG requires no additional training or supervision for its generation framework. Evaluations cover cross-domain few-shot detection, remote sensing, and camouflaged objects. The authors report consistent gains over strong baselines and new state-of-the-art results. These findings support retrieval-guided background synthesis as a useful augmentation strategy when object identity and environmental appearance both matter, particularly where few labeled examples leave little room for category or domain mismatches.
neurips-2025-domain-rag-retrieval-guided.tldr: Domain-RAG preserves foreground objects and generates retrieval-guided backgrounds to improve few-shot detection across visual domains.

paragraphs: Novel view synthesis creates images of a scene from viewpoints beyond those originally observed. Gaussian splatting offers efficient rendering, but its two-dimensional and three-dimensional forms have different strengths. The abstract describes 3D Gaussians as strong at appearance detail but weaker at multi-view geometric consistency, while 2D Gaussians favor consistency at the expense of texture.

EGGS combines both forms in a hybrid scene representation. A unified rasterization method renders the mixed representation, and an adaptive exchange mechanism allows elements to change between 2D and 3D types. A frequency-decoupled optimization procedure helps exploit their respective strengths. This makes the balance between geometry and appearance part of the representation and its training process.

The implementation uses CUDA acceleration for efficient training and inference. Across the reported experiments, EGGS improves rendering quality, geometric accuracy, and efficiency relative to existing methods. These findings indicate that combining and adapting Gaussian types can address the tradeoff described in the paper, supporting novel views that preserve visual detail while representing scene geometry more accurately.
neurips-2025-eggs-exchangeable-2d-3d-gau.tldr: EGGS dynamically combines 2D and 3D Gaussians to improve the balance between scene geometry, visual detail, and rendering efficiency.

paragraphs: Diffusion models generate images through repeated denoising, making inference speed and accumulated error central concerns. EVODiff studies this process through information theory. The paper argues that successful reverse transitions reduce conditional entropy, meaning that each transition should reduce uncertainty about the cleaner result given the current state.

This perspective leads to two stated insights: predicting clean data performs better than predicting noise, and optimizing conditional variance provides a reference-free way to reduce transition and reconstruction errors. EVODiff turns these ideas into a denoising method that optimizes conditional entropy. The aim is to improve the information gained during the generation process while reducing uncertainty.

Experiments report consistent improvements over state-of-the-art gradient-based solvers. Against DPM-Solver++, the abstract reports up to 45.5% lower reconstruction error on CIFAR-10 at ten function evaluations, with FID changing from 5.10 to 2.78. On ImageNet-256, high-quality sampling uses fifteen rather than twenty evaluations. Text-to-image results also show improvements and fewer artifacts, supporting the method across multiple image-generation settings.
neurips-2025-evodiff-entropy-aware-varia.tldr: EVODiff improves diffusion inference by using conditional entropy and variance to guide more accurate, efficient denoising.

paragraphs: Code generators can produce plausible programs without using execution feedback during generation. Execution-Guided Classifier-Free Guidance, or EG-CFG, brings that feedback into the process line by line. The goal is to make observed program behavior influence subsequent generation, giving the model information about whether its candidate code works against test cases.

For each line, the method uses beam search to sample candidate program completions. It executes those candidates against tests, extracts signals from the results, and incorporates the signals into the generation prompt. Guidance stays consistent across tokens within a line and is refreshed at line boundaries. This timing is intended to keep the feedback coherent while preserving syntactic structure.

The approach also supports multiple agents working in parallel on different reasoning paths, producing a broader collection of candidate solutions. Experiments span foundational coding problems, competitive programming, and data science tasks. The authors report significant improvements over standard approaches and state-of-the-art results across these settings. The findings support execution feedback as an effective source of guidance during code construction.
neurips-2025-execution-guided-line-by-li.tldr: EG-CFG uses test-execution feedback at line boundaries to guide code generation toward better-performing programs.

paragraphs: A humanoid controller must handle movements with very different demands on the whole body. Combining them in one training process can introduce conflicting control requirements and mismatched data distributions. BumbleBee addresses this difficulty by first organizing and learning specialized behaviors, then combining the resulting expertise into a general controller.

An autoencoder-based clustering method groups behaviorally similar motions using both motion features and descriptions. Each cluster receives an expert policy. Those experts are then refined with real-world data through iterative delta action modeling, which helps address differences between simulated and physical behavior. Finally, the refined experts are distilled into a single generalist controller.

This sequence makes motion grouping and adaptation to the real robot part of the route to general control. Experiments in two simulations and on a physical humanoid report state-of-the-art whole-body control, with agility and robustness across the motion types considered. The results support the framework's strategy of learning compatible behavior groups before consolidation, while using real-world feedback to improve the expertise being transferred.
neurips-2025-from-experts-to-a-generalis.tldr: BumbleBee clusters motions, adapts specialist policies with real-world data, and distills them into one agile humanoid controller.

paragraphs: Neural networks can contain many parameters while their weight matrices have approximately low rank, meaning that their transformations use fewer independent directions than their size suggests. This paper asks how that structure affects generalization guarantees. Its bounds explicitly exploit approximate low rank when it is present in the network.

The analysis uses Schatten p quasi norms of the weight matrices, which allow the bounds to reflect different aspects of matrix structure. For small p, the stated sample complexity scales as W times r times L squared, up to logarithmic factors, where W is width, r is weight-matrix rank, and L is depth. As p increases, the result becomes more like a norm-based bound.

The proof connects parameter-based and norm-based analyses through careful interpolation. Experiments show the resulting bound improving on both classic parameter counting and norm-based bounds in a typical overparametrised regime. The significance is a more informative theoretical description of networks with low-rank structure: their apparent size need not be the only quantity used to assess generalization.
neurips-2025-generalization-bounds-for-r.tldr: The paper derives generalization bounds that exploit approximately low-rank weights and improve on conventional bounds in reported overparametrised settings.

paragraphs: In fully decentralized cooperative learning, each agent sees states, its own actions, and shared rewards, but not other agents' actions. As teammates learn, the environment perceived by one agent changes. Value estimates can also undervalue coordinated actions when those actions are assessed across differing teammate behavior. Return-Aware Context addresses both problems.

RAC treats the locally perceived task as a contextual Markov decision process, with different contexts representing different joint policies. It assumes the joint policy changes only between episodes. Under that assumption, the method uses discretized episode returns to distinguish contexts and learns a value function conditioned on them. This gives agents a way to account for changing team behavior through shared outcomes.

For action evaluation, RAC constructs an optimistic marginal value intended to encourage optimal joint actions and mitigate relative overgeneralization. Evaluations on matrix games, predator-and-prey tasks, and SMAC support its effectiveness. The approach matters because it uses information already available to decentralized agents to address both changing local dynamics and the difficulty of recognizing valuable coordination.
neurips-2025-in-context-fully-decentrali.tldr: RAC uses episode-return contexts and optimistic value estimates to improve cooperation without observing other agents' actions.

paragraphs: This paper applies gauge-equivariant neural networks to predicting Chern numbers, topological invariants of multiband topological insulators. Gauge symmetry allows a different transformation at each point, making it substantially richer than a global symmetry shared across all points. The architecture incorporates this local symmetry into the prediction process.

The abstract states that the network's gauge symmetry guarantees a topologically invariant prediction. A practical obstacle is that the relevant architectures suffer from training instabilities, severe enough to prevent training for larger gauge groups. The authors introduce a normalization layer that preserves gauge equivariance while stabilizing learning, allowing the symmetry-based model to be trained successfully.

The paper also proves a universal approximation theorem for its model. In experiments, training uses only samples with trivial Chern number, yet the model generalizes to samples with nontrivial Chern number. This result supports the value of the architecture's structural constraints in the tested setting. The theoretical approximation result, normalization method, and generalization experiments together address expressiveness, trainability, and prediction beyond the training examples' topological class.
neurips-2025-learning-chern-numbers-of-m.tldr: A stabilizing gauge-equivariant normalization layer enables Chern-number prediction that generalizes from trivial to nontrivial training-unseen topology.

paragraphs: Linear inverse problems reconstruct an underlying signal from measurements, potentially corrupted by noise. Diffusion models can support reconstruction, but existing approaches often alternate denoising with many projection steps that enforce agreement with the measurements. CDIM makes this constraint-handling process adaptive to reduce the work required during inference.

The method adjusts both the number and size of projection steps. Its target is to align the residual measurement energy with the theoretical distribution induced by forward diffusion. That alignment provides a criterion for maintaining measurement consistency as denoising progresses. The authors report a tenfold to fiftyfold reduction in projection steps while substantially accelerating constrained inference.

For noise-free linear problems, CDIM exactly meets the measurement constraints using few projection steps, including cases where existing methods fail. Evaluations cover super-resolution, denoising, inpainting, deblurring, and reprojection of 3D point clouds. These results demonstrate the approach across different reconstruction tasks, with its central contribution being a more economical way to coordinate diffusion-based denoising and the constraints imposed by observed measurements.
neurips-2025-linearly-constrained-diffus.tldr: CDIM adaptively enforces measurement consistency in diffusion reconstruction, reducing projection steps by 10–50×.

paragraphs: A multimodal classifier can depend too heavily on its strongest input modality and fail to use information available elsewhere. MIDAS addresses this imbalance through data augmentation. It creates examples whose modalities carry semantically inconsistent information, forcing training to confront disagreement between the input sources rather than always seeing mutually supportive signals.

The augmented examples receive labels based on confidence scores from individual modalities. Because that procedure can still favor the more confident source, MIDAS dynamically increases the loss weight associated with the least confident modality. This weak-modality weighting is designed to make the contradictory examples useful for learning from sources the model would otherwise underuse.

A second weighting mechanism prioritizes misaligned examples whose features resemble aligned examples. These cases are harder to distinguish and provide more challenging class-discrimination signals. Experiments across multiple multimodal classification benchmarks report significant improvements over related baselines in addressing modality imbalance. The method's contribution is the combination of deliberately inconsistent training examples and targeted weighting that directs learning toward weaker modalities and ambiguous cases.
neurips-2025-midas-misalignment-based-da.tldr: MIDAS combines deliberately mismatched modalities with adaptive loss weighting to reduce overreliance on dominant inputs.

paragraphs: Drone active tracking requires a drone to move in response to visual observations so that it can keep following a target. Complex surroundings and frequent interference make this difficult for reinforcement learning. The paper contributes both a benchmark for evaluating the task and a learning method intended to improve tracking in such environments.

The DAT benchmark includes 24 city-scale scenes, targets with human-like behavior, and high-fidelity dynamics simulation. A digital twin tool supports additional scene generation. The proposed method, GC-VAT, uses a goal-centered reward to give the agent feedback across viewpoints, supporting a wider range of perception and movement. Curriculum-based training progressively develops tracking performance in complex environments.

Experiments using simulation and real-world images report superior performance for GC-VAT, including approximately 72% tracking success in the simulator. That number specifically describes the simulated evaluation. The benchmark and method together provide a framework for studying how visual feedback, reward design, and progressive training affect active tracking amid varied scenes and interference.
neurips-2025-open-world-drone-active-tra.tldr: The paper introduces the DAT drone-tracking benchmark and GC-VAT, whose goal-centered rewards and curriculum achieve about 72% simulated tracking success.

paragraphs: Panoramic video generation must create a coherent scene across an entire 360-degree view. Adapting conventional text-to-video models is difficult because panoramic imagery has different spatial structure, and suitable training data are limited. PanoWan addresses both issues while retaining the generative knowledge available in pretrained video models.

The method adds a small set of mechanisms tailored to panoramic coordinates. Latitude-aware sampling addresses distortion associated with latitude. Rotated semantic denoising and padded pixel-wise decoding handle the longitude boundary, where the panorama must join seamlessly. These changes target the geometric features that distinguish panoramic generation from conventional video generation.

The authors also introduce PanoVid, a captioned panoramic video dataset covering diverse scenarios, to support learning the adapted representations. PanoWan achieves reported state-of-the-art panoramic video generation performance and shows robustness on zero-shot downstream tasks. The contribution combines targeted model adaptation with additional training data, offering a way to transfer existing video-generation capabilities to immersive content while addressing distortion and boundary continuity.
neurips-2025-panowan-lifting-diffusion-v.tldr: PanoWan adapts pretrained video diffusion models to seamless 360-degree generation using panoramic-coordinate mechanisms and the new PanoVid dataset.

paragraphs: Speech systems for Indian languages often lack training data representing the dialects people actually speak. RESPIN-S1.0 addresses this gap with validated read speech across nine languages and more than 38 dialects. Its agriculture and finance focus adds domain diversity alongside linguistic diversity, targeting areas highlighted as important in the paper.

Native dialect speakers composed the text, which passed automated and manual validation. Contributors recorded more than 200,000 distinct sentences through a mobile crowdsourcing platform. Recordings are grouped into clean, semi-noisy, and noisy subsets according to transcription quality, with the clean subset alone exceeding 10,000 hours. The resource also includes phonetic lexicons that account for dialect, speaker metadata, and reproducible training, development, and test splits.

The authors benchmark several speech-recognition approaches, including TDNN-HMM, E-Branchformer, Whisper, and wav2vec2-based models. Fine-tuning on RESPIN significantly improves recognition accuracy over pretrained baselines. The corpus therefore contributes both training material and a shared evaluation resource for dialect-aware recognition, language identification, and related speech technologies serving digitally underserved language communities.
neurips-2025-respin-s1-0-a-read-speech-c.tldr: RESPIN-S1.0 provides over 10,000 hours of clean read speech across nine Indian languages and more than 38 dialects, improving recognition through fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Online bilevel optimization involves an outer optimization problem that depends on an inner one, with both objectives changing over time. Existing approaches use regret measures smoothed over time windows. Such smoothing may obscure performance when the underlying functions change rapidly, motivating guarantees that assess stochastic bilevel regret without that temporal averaging.

The authors introduce a search direction usable by both first-order methods and zeroth-order methods. First-order methods use derivative information, while zeroth-order methods estimate needed quantities from function evaluations. Algorithms built around the new direction achieve sublinear stochastic bilevel regret without window smoothing. Sublinear growth means accumulated regret grows more slowly than the time horizon under the paper's analysis.

The framework also reduces oracle dependence when estimating hypergradients, updates inner and outer variables alongside a linear-system solution, and uses zeroth-order estimates of gradients, Hessians, and Jacobians. Experiments on online parametric loss tuning and black-box adversarial attacks validate the approach. These contributions connect an unsmoothed theoretical performance measure with computational changes intended to make evolving nested optimization more efficient.
neurips-2025-stochastic-regret-guarantee.tldr: A new search direction enables first- and zeroth-order online bilevel methods with sublinear stochastic regret without window smoothing.

paragraphs: Speech language models need tokenizers that turn audio into compact sequences while retaining useful speech information. TaDiCodec addresses the complexity of designs that rely on multiple quantization layers, high frame rates, auxiliary pretrained models, or separate training stages. It brings quantization and reconstruction together in a diffusion autoencoder trained end to end.

Text guidance enters the diffusion decoder to improve reconstruction and compression. For 24 kHz speech, the model uses a single-layer codebook at 6.25 frames per second and a bitrate of 0.0875 kbps. The authors report superior results on word error rate, speaker similarity, and estimated speech quality, showing that the compact representation supports several important aspects of speech reconstruction.

Training takes place in one stage without auxiliary pretrained models. The tokenizer is also evaluated in zero-shot text-to-speech systems using both autoregressive and masked generative language modeling. These experiments show compatibility with both approaches and a small reconstruction-generation gap. That finding connects codec reconstruction performance to its usefulness when a language model must generate the speech tokens.
neurips-2025-tadicodec-text-aware-diffus.tldr: TaDiCodec uses text-guided diffusion to produce compact speech tokens with single-stage training and strong reconstruction and generation results.

paragraphs: Understanding a language model's input space requires checking whether token embeddings have the geometric structure an analysis assumes. This paper develops a statistical test for local smoothness and relative flatness around individual tokens. Its null hypothesis uses a smooth fiber bundle, a structure that generalizes a manifold with boundary.

The test has an important asymmetry: rejecting the null at a token indicates an irregularity in that token's neighborhood, while failing to reject it is uninformative. Applied to several open-source language models with different embeddings, the test frequently rejects the null. The authors interpret this as evidence that the token subspace is neither a fiber bundle nor a manifold.

The paper connects these geometric findings to response stability. For two semantically equivalent prompts, it states that the one containing a token implicated by the test will likely produce less stable responses. This is a qualified prediction about stability, not a claim that every flagged token inevitably causes failure. The contribution is both a local diagnostic and evidence challenging smooth geometric assumptions about token embeddings.
neurips-2025-token-embeddings-violate-th.tldr: A statistical test finds frequent local irregularities in token embeddings, challenging manifold assumptions and suggesting reduced stability for prompts containing implicated tokens.

paragraphs: Virtual try-on models can generate convincing clothing images while still missing details or visual qualities that users care about. This paper addresses that mismatch by collecting generated try-on images with human judgments across multiple perceptual criteria. Those annotations train VTON-VLLM, a vision-language model that evaluates results and helps guide their improvement.

VTON-VLLM contributes to synthesis in two ways. During training, it supplies detailed supervision for a plug-and-play refinement model. During inference, it enables adaptive, preference-aware test-time scaling. These roles use the learned assessment of human preferences at different stages of the system, extending its function beyond producing an automatic evaluation of a finished image.

The authors also introduce VITON-Bench, which includes complex try-on scenarios, together with metrics that account for human preferences. Extensive experiments report markedly better alignment with those preferences when VTON-VLLM supports existing try-on models. The combined contribution links human annotations, automated evaluation, model refinement, and inference-time adaptation around the same perceptual goals, providing a more holistic way to assess and improve virtual try-on.
neurips-2025-vton-vllm-aligning-virtual-.tldr: VTON-VLLM learns from human judgments to evaluate and improve virtual try-on images through refinement training and preference-aware inference.

paragraphs: Emotional speech synthesis often assigns an expressive style to an entire utterance, even though emotion and speaking rate can change within a sentence. WeSCon adds word-level control to a pretrained zero-shot text-to-speech model. It addresses the scarcity of annotated examples containing transitions in emotion or speed within a single sentence.

The framework first guides the pretrained model through a multi-round inference process. Transition smoothing helps manage changes in expression, while a dynamic speed mechanism controls speaking rate. It then introduces a dynamic emotional attention bias and uses self-training to fine-tune the model. This turns the initial guided process into end-to-end word-level expressive control with simpler inference.

The method does not rely on datasets containing the intra-sentence transitions it aims to produce. Experiments report state-of-the-art word-level emotional control while retaining the original model's strong zero-shot synthesis capabilities. The result matters because it connects finer control over individual words with preservation of an existing synthesis model's capabilities, using self-training to overcome a specific annotation shortage.
neurips-2025-word-level-emotional-expres.tldr: WeSCon uses self-training to add word-level emotion and speed control to zero-shot speech synthesis without annotated within-sentence transition data.
